thread:
maya: FYI mkdocs linkcheck flagged anchors after the MDX -> mkdocs migration; looks like some headings split on 
line breaks and slugify differs.

kevin: any concrete example?

maya: on guides/migration/upgrade.md a heading `## CI & deploy pipelines` was wrapped by the formatter to:
```
## CI
& deploy pipelines
```
Some builds produced `#ci--deploy-pipelines`, others `#ci-deploy-pipelines` so cross-page links are flaky.

ops-bot: linkcheck: 9 broken anchors found in docs/guides/migration/*.md

frank: idea: normalize headings before wrapping — collapse whitespace and replace `&` with `and`. Also strip stray punctuation.

nina: agree. we should also make the link resolver in linkcheck try candidate slugs: original, spaces->-, ampersand->and. avoids noisy failures while we fix sources.

maya: pushed a tiny migration util patch and linkcheck tweak: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4199

kevin: paste the helper?

maya: `def norm(h): return re.sub(r"\s+"," ",h).replace("&","and").strip()`

frank: can you add a unit test for slug(norm(...)) == "ci-and-deploy-pipelines"?

maya: added test in the PR. CI linkcheck drops from 9 -> 2 locally. Remaining ones are legacy notebooks with soft wraps.

ops-bot: ci/linkcheck started for PR #4199

kevin: LGTM, merge when green. Add a short note in the migration guide about header normalization so external contributors know the behavior.

maya: done, merged, docs deploy queued.

ops-bot: deploy: docs site build complete, published https://docs.redwood.ai/release/2026-03-23

nina: spot-checked anchors; looks stable. closing. :shipit:
